tasks.title: Loop v2.1 V2-02: freeze the verifier with a manifest hash and a safe re-verify path

created_by.name: Claude Code (VS Code)
created_by.session_ref: Loop v2.1 V2-01 and V2-05 build session, 2026-10-06

tasks.source_evidence: The Loop v2.1 design (private notes) counts 5 incidents in 2 days where a verifier or a fixture it reads changed during a run and the run still passed unrecorded. delegate.ps1 hashes nothing today: a verifier edited mid-run, or a fixture it imports, changes what accepted means with no trace. V2-01 (cf-lab PR 9) added per-attempt rows and reserved the states blocked and accepted-after-verifier-edit for this task.

roi.rationale: Estimate: an accepted result is only worth what its verifier is worth; hashing everything the verifier uses makes a changed verifier visible and blocks the run, and a recorded safe path keeps legitimate fixes possible.

tasks.acceptance: delegate.ps1 copies the verifier's manifest (the verifier, its directory tree minus caches, and any -VerifierFiles; the layout is kept relative to their common ancestor), hashes the copy (raw bytes, plus a line-ending-normalised hash for comparing across checkouts) and compares it with the live files before every verifier run, after it, and immediately before writing accepted. The candidate is hashed per attempt and is not part of the frozen set, so a changing candidate never blocks. A change mid-run exits 3 with state blocked, no accepted row and the output file restored (tests: a fixture, a -VerifierFiles file, a new file, and a line-ending-only change). Before the first model call a pre-flight runs the verifier in the copy on an empty stub: exit 0 is refused (it cannot fail); a missing-file or import error is refused and names the path; any other failure passes (a test with a verifier that raises on an empty stub). A -ReverifyOf <run id> path re-proves the new verifier on the empty stub (must fail), the unchanged original (must pass; skipped and recorded if there is none) and the previously rejected candidate (must still fail; skipped and recorded if there is none), records the old and new hashes and a diff of path and hash lists (never contents), ends only in accepted-after-verifier-edit, and a person reads the diff. Refused at start: an output file inside the verifier tree, symlinks or junctions in it, and a manifest above the stated caps. Negative tests pin the limits: an absolute-path read, and a loop over a missing directory, are NOT refused. The only claim made anywhere is: it detects changes to the declared verifier files between the proof and acceptance, and refuses before the first call a verifier whose empty-stub run reaches a relative path outside its manifest; it is not a sandbox. lint-powershell.ps1 is clean on delegate.ps1 and every existing test passes.
tasks.notes: Proposed by a model; only a human moves it to ready. Full tier: a blind different-family challenger on the hashing logic, then a person reads the diff. Open design decision for the maintainer: how a read outside the manifest is detected (run the verifier in a copy of its manifest, as verify-in-copy.py does, is the candidate). Controller-built, not delegated: it edits the harness. | Design reviewed by a blind council on 2026-10-07 (Opus, Fable, Qwen3.8 27B, Gemma 4 31B; the controller's own view was written first): all four said adopt with changes. Flags were confirmed by reproduction, including a vacuous-pass case the controller had missed: an incomplete manifest copy plus a verifier that loops over a missing directory is accepted although the full verifier would fail it, and the empty-stub pre-flight cannot see it. The acceptance above is the revised one. Still for the maintainer: approve moving to ready; the caps (proposal: 500 files, 20 MB); and that verifiers which reach into sibling folders must name them with -VerifierFiles. | 2026-10-07 later: the maintainer answered yes ("Yeah, go for it") to the question whether to set this ready with the council's caps (500 files, 20 MB), so it was built the same day in cf-lab on branch loop/v2-02-verifier-freeze; it stays in_progress until the pull request is merged and a person has read the diff (Full tier). Verifiers that reach sibling folders must name them with -VerifierFiles. Review: a blind challenger pass by two cloud models (Opus, Fable) and the local Qwen; each finding was reproduced or refuted before anything was changed, and the fixes have tests. For the maintainer to approve, three places where the build differs from the revised acceptance above: (1) the pre-flight does not refuse every missing-file, import or command error on the empty stub, because "The term is not recognized" and "cannot import name" are how ordinary verifiers fail on an empty file; it refuses exit 0, a path that exists beside the live verifier but is not in the copy, a Python module that cannot be imported, and an interpreter that cannot start. (2) A verifier that writes to or removes the candidate blocks the run (candidate-changed); a candidate that differs from one attempt to the next never blocks. (3) -ReverifyOf also needs the earlier run's manifest, the same verifier file and at least one earlier output to re-prove against; the output file from before the run must get the same verdict the old verifier gave it (recorded at the start of that run), not a pass; and an edit that loosens the verifier (accepts what it rejected) has no safe path by design. Mutation proof: 40 one-line mutants of the new code, each run against the new tests; 35 were caught. The five that survived: the two looks immediately before accepted and before accepted-after-verifier-edit (each repeats the look just before it, so removing it changes no result a test can see), a path on another drive counted as a hole, a path beside the candidate counted as a hole (the stub now sits in a folder of its own, which makes the check redundant), and hash sets that fold case on every platform (only visible on Linux, where the tests were not run). | 2026-10-07 later: merged as cf-lab PR 18 (squash). Follow-ups from the same work: delegate-batch improvements (dry run, resume, priority, dependencies; cf-lab PR 20) and a loop-report line for the two new states (in PR 18). The row stays in_progress for the maintainer to close; the three differences from the revised acceptance listed above stand until the maintainer approves them.
